entities.name: Missouri Botanical Garden
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Missouri Botanical Garden, established in 1859 in St. Louis, Missouri, stands as a pivotal institution in the realm of botanical research and conservation. Founded by Henry Shaw, a prominent businessman and philanthropist, the garden has evolved into one of the foremost botanical research centers in the world, contributing significantly to the understanding and preservation of plant biodiversity. Spanning 79 acres, it houses over 6,000 species of plants, making it an invaluable resource for both scholars and the general public, who seek to understand the complexities of plant life and its ecological significance.

During its early years, the Missouri Botanical Garden played a crucial role in the study and classification of plants, particularly through its living collections and herbarium, which contains over 7.5 million specimens. The garden has facilitated extensive research and outreach programs, fostering an appreciation for horticulture and environmental conservation. Notably, it was instrumental in the development of the concept of sustainable gardening practices, influencing both amateur and professional horticulturists alike. In addition, the garden has been involved in numerous international conservation efforts, working collaboratively with various global organizations to combat plant extinction.

The legacy of the Missouri Botanical Garden extends far beyond its immediate contributions; it has inspired the establishment of similar institutions across the United States and worldwide. Its educational programs have shaped public awareness regarding the importance of biodiversity and the need for conservation, impacting generations of students and researchers. The garden's dedication to scientific inquiry and environmental stewardship continues to resonate, as it serves as a model for integrating research with community engagement and conservation efforts.
